context:
Goal: q_max batch runs finish sooner without wasting runner minutes.
In plain words: q_max CI has a cheap `checks` job (lint and similar) and a bigger `test` job. Today `test` starts only after `checks` passes (decision D-718, the spend gate: do not spend test minutes on a change the cheap checks already reject).
Correction (runner 11 read q_max's checks.yml, 12:22 CST): q_max has only ONE kind of CI run. checks.yml runs only on a batch PR head and on a push to main; lane PRs run no full CI. So the old option c (together on the batch run, cheap first on lane runs) has nothing to split, and I removed it. Also my earlier answer 'they are independent' was wrong as built: `test` has `needs: [checks]`, so a red `checks` skips `test`, it does not run it.
Problem (rule): starting both together finishes sooner, but a red `checks` would then still spend the `test` minutes, which D-718 exists to avoid. Starting them together also needs a small change in q_max's CI file (move the values `test` reads from `checks` to a small scope job).
Based on (ruling): q_max D-718 ci-spend-gate; claude-settings ci-once-per-batch (your 21:16 CST Nov 12).
Based on (read): runner 11, q_max origin/main .github/workflows/checks.yml, 12:22 CST Nov 13.
Departs from: q_max main, where `test` always starts after `checks` — a starts both together on the batch run.

options.gain: Wall time about 15 to 10 min (projection, unmeasured).
options.how: q_max starts `test` beside `checks` on the batch run (its only full run); `test` stops waiting on `checks`.
options.label: Start both together on the batch run
options.lose: A red `checks` still spends the `test` minutes.

options.gain: A red `checks` never spends `test` minutes; no CI file change.
options.how: q_max keeps D-718 as it is.
options.label: Keep cheap first

title: In q_max, should the `test` job start together with `checks` on the batch run, or keep waiting for `checks`?
why: Goes against q_max D-718, which needs your word.
